power_for_place.why: A's progression better matches tier jobs. B distributes substantial scaling too early. Estimates below use normal copies with good setup and credit only the named card's contribution.

A_outliers.issue: An extra Glopgut trigger adds 20–24 permanent stats across 5–6 Ogres: roughly 4× the 5.5 benchmark.
Five consumed types grant six Ogres 180 combat stats, over 2× 80. One All-type meal trivialises the diversity requirement.

B_outliers.issue: Five occupied Bellies bank 20 stats each turn versus 2. Delayed access insufficiently compensates for a 10× rate.
Three bursts yield 18 combat stats versus 4.5: 4×.
Four Belly types across six Ogres yield 48 permanent stats per turn versus 20: 2.4×.
Digesting a 20/20 with Gourmand grants two others 160 additional permanent stats versus 53: 3× under the written rules.

power_for_place.A_tier_jobs: Early food and threshold tools lead into composition enablers, then multipliers and capstones. Ritualist arrives prematurely.
power_for_place.B_tier_jobs: Early stocking tools work, but Cook and Crier deliver later-tier output. Upper tiers multiply already generous engines.

distinctiveness.why: B makes storage, borrowed abilities and eventual release one recurring decision. Its Magnetic/Reborn echoes become a distinct play pattern.
distinctiveness.A_core: Attack-threshold sequencing and Recruit-phase Deathrattle harvesting distinguish an otherwise Demon-adjacent consumption engine.
distinctiveness.B_core: Keep text and a reserve body, or Digest for stats and capacity; borrowed types broaden that decision.

A_has_B_lost: Green Grog, Bickering Ogre Magus and Bloodmaul Goader create concrete threshold puzzles. Meat-Picker and The Butcher redistribute resources through Leftovers.
B_has_A_lost: Cook banks future bodies; Bottomless rescues overflow summons; Gladiator captures enemies. These preserve useful minions instead of converting everything irreversibly into stats.
